I0.label: No newly released risk information
I0.controller_input: training stationary distribution propagated at the native monthly frequency

IF.label: Current filtered risk only
IF.controller_input: latest legally released filtered high-risk belief repeated at the lead coordinate

IL.label: Released lead-aligned forecast
IL.controller_input: latest legally released alpha multiplied by P to the calendar-month distance from source month to readiness maturity

ORACLE.label: Perfect information oracle
ORACLE.controller_input: realized current disruption state and realized readiness-maturity disruption state

GH.label: Historical release
GH.construction: canonical 5.2.1 public release dates and historical event physical path

GT.label: Minimally sufficient true release
GT.construction: move the last event-pre information packet to event onset minus readiness lead so g_R equals zero

GL.label: Insufficient lead
GL.construction: move the same packet to the first Monday after the g_R equals zero boundary

GFW.label: False warning
GFW.construction: use GT release timing with the matched normal-demand path and serviceability fixed at one

controller.common_seed_rule: inherit the three frozen 5.2.2 seed indices; new conditions use the same deterministic initialization namespace
controller.il_rd_anchor: reuse the accepted 5.2.2 BC and constrained-SAC checkpoint pairs because they are the already-trained proposed architecture under released lead information and full rights
controller.new_condition_training: from-scratch BC teacher fitting and constrained SAC optimization under the condition-specific information or rights interface

timing.preparation_window_rule: exactly L_R Mondays ending one week before event onset
timing.insufficient_release_rule: first Monday after the sufficient boundary
timing.historical_anchor_rule: the accepted 21-week 5.2.2 event-window replay is evaluated separately from the designed preparation-window stresses

statistics.multiplicity_adjustment: Holm adjusted paired p-values plus within-family simultaneous t intervals

computation.basis: training uses four isolated workers with four numerical-library threads; Python-bound matched evaluation uses fourteen one-thread workers and reserves two of sixteen logical processors for orchestration and the operating system

figures.medoid_rule: standardized total blocked mass, peak blocked mass, mean serviceability, minimum serviceability, and recovery rate; policy outcomes excluded
